## 1. LOCATION OVERVIEW
SYNTHETIC TEST DOSSIER. Not real research: every fact and URL below is made up to exercise the parser and the allocation checks. Testville is a mid sized city with a mix of Victorian terraces, interwar semis and large post war plots on the northern edge [https://example.gov.uk/overview].

## 2. NEIGHBOURHOOD PROFILES
### [TST-N01] Northfield Heath | neighbourhood
Profile: Detached houses on plots of around a third of an acre, many with mature trees and sloping rear gardens [https://example.gov.uk/northfield]. Gardens here generate terracing, retaining walls and large lawn renovations (inferred).
Linked issues: TST-I01, TST-I02

### TST-N02 | Old Riverside | neighbourhood
Profile: Victorian villas on a clay terrace above the river, with long narrow gardens and original boundary walls [https://example.gov.uk/riverside]. Part of the area is a conservation area (see TST-R01).
Linked issues: TST-I01

### [TST-N03] Dockside Trading Estate | estate
Profile: Mostly warehouses, trade counters and car parks, with a small block of flats on the eastern edge [https://example.gov.uk/dockside].
Linked issues: TST-I03

### [TST-N04] Westmead | neighbourhood
Profile: Interwar semis with medium gardens. Little verifiable detail was found for this area (inferred).
Linked issues: TST-I02

### [TST-N05] Eastbrook | village
Profile: A former village absorbed into the city in the 1960s, with bungalows on wide plots and shared verges [https://example.gov.uk/eastbrook] (dated: March 2026).
Linked issues: TST-I02

## 3. LOCAL ISSUES
### [TST-I01] Slow draining clay ground
Detail: Heavy clay under much of the north and the river terrace holds water for days after rain, so patios and lawns on it pond [https://example.gov.uk/geology]. It affects TST-N01 and TST-N02 most.
Scope: Local
Category tags: Landscape Gardener, Paving contractor, Lawn care service
Service tags: Drainage, Patio laying
Angles:
- Cause: clay sub soil with a high water table in winter.
- Timing: worst from November to March.
Condition question: Why does my garden stay wet for days?
Answer material: Clay holds water. A sub base and a fall away from the house help.

### [TST-I02] Mature trees and protected trees
Detail: Many plots carry mature oaks, several under tree preservation orders, which limits root work near them [https://example.gov.uk/tpo]. Affects TST-N01, TST-N04 and TST-N05.
Scope: District
Category tags: Tree service, Landscape Gardener
Service tags: Tree surgery
Angles:
- Rules: work on a protected tree needs council consent.
Condition question: Can I cut back my neighbour's oak?
Answer material: Overhanging branches can usually be cut back to the boundary unless the tree is protected.

### [TST-I03] Tidal flooding on the waterfront
Detail: Low lying ground near the docks floods on spring tides [https://example.gov.uk/flood].
Scope: Local
Category tags: Roofing contractor
Service tags: Flood repair
Angles:
- Timing: spring tides and storm surges.
Condition question: Is my street at risk of flooding?
Answer material: Streets near the dock wall are in flood zone 3.

## 5. RULES & COUNCIL
### [TST-R01] Old Riverside Conservation Area
Detail: Boundary walls and front gardens are protected; removing a front wall to create parking needs consent [https://example.gov.uk/conservation].
Applies to: TST-N02

### [TST-R02] Tree preservation orders
Detail: Several hundred trees across the north are protected [https://example.gov.uk/tpo].
Applies to: whole area

## 6. DEMAND BY AREA
Larger plots in TST-N01 suit landscape design and paving; TST-N02 suits wall repair and lawn care [https://example.gov.uk/demand].
